topic.title: Feature Selection, Stability, and Informative Subsets
topic.overview: Feature selection identifies which measured variables are sufficient for useful prediction or representation. The cluster includes kernel-space selection, unsupervised scoring, redundancy-aware methods, and stability analysis. Related work asks which data sources best support a shared representation, extending selection from coordinates to the evidence used to learn them.
topic.whyItMatters: Reducing inputs can lower acquisition cost and improve interpretability, but unstable selections can give misleading scientific conclusions. A small subset should retain useful information and remain reasonably consistent under changes in the sample.
topic.evolution: The earliest representatives develop practical and non-greedy selection strategies. Later methods exploit manifold or kernel structure and dependencies among features. More recent work emphasizes generalization guarantees, bagging-based stability, and source screening, including cases where discarding seemingly relevant data improves shared-subspace estimation.
openQuestions: How should selection report uncertainty when several correlated subsets work equally well?
Can stability be improved without hiding genuinely heterogeneous signals?
